notes.text:
Chronological Paradox in the it-Engine (Engine Defect)
Step: #38
Sūtras involved: 1.3.4 न विभक्तौ तुस्माः, 1.4.104 विभक्तिश्च.
Issue: The UI header at #38 indicates the engine used 1.3.4 to prevent 1.3.3 from deleting the final 'm' of am. However, 1.3.4 specifically protects letters only when they are part of an affix carrying the vibhakti designation. In this trace, the vibhakti saṃjñā is never formally assigned (1.4.104 is missing), and even if it were, saṃjñā assignments occur after step #38 (e.g., #58).
Classification: Engine defect. The engine is violating Engine Principle #1 and #2. The it-module is reading a hardcoded, dictionary-level is_vibhakti boolean attached to the sup affix rather than waiting for the linguistic state machine to declare it legally via 1.4.104.
notes.verdict: Claude 2026-11-16 — REPEAT of note 1.4.104 bc05da723d, already ledgered under S179: sutra_1_3_4.py reads a predicate (is_vibhakti_upadesha) and 1.4.102–104 are not explicit rows before it. The 'chronological paradox' is that same gap, not a new defect. No separate work; reopen only with new evidence.
